title: Finisar’s (FNSR) “Buy” Rating Reaffirmed at William Blair
text:
Finisar’s (FNSR) “Buy” Rating Reaffirmed at William Blair Posted by Anthony Miller | Mar 27th, 2018 
William Blair reaffirmed their buy rating on shares of Finisar (NASDAQ:FNSR) in a report issued on Monday, March 5th. 
“We expect the company to come in roughly in line on revenue with a downward bias to EPS due to ongoing datacom pricing pressure affecting gross margin. The Street is looking for $333 million on revenue (roughly flat sequentially) and $0.23 for EPS; we are in line on revenue and a penny below consensus on EPS. We believe the company could see modest quarter-over-quarter expansion in 3-D sensing (revenue is relatively small to be affected by recent Apple [AAPL $176.21; Not Rated] iPhoneX cuts) offsetting ongoing inventory correction in China (at Huawei and ZTE) and product transition at hyperscale customers (Amazon [AMZN $1,500.25; Outperform] transitioning from 40G to 100G). The biggest risk to Finisar remains gross margins, which could remain pressured until datacom pricing stabilizes, cost reduction products become available, and/or higher-margin products (CFP2-ACO and ROADMs) begin to ship in volume.”,” William Blair’s analyst commented. A number of other research firms also recently commented on FNSR. Raymond James Financial set a $22.00 price objective on Finisar and gave the stock a buy rating in a research note on Wednesday, December 13th. ValuEngine raised Finisar from a hold rating to a buy rating in a research note on Thursday, December 14th. Craig Hallum set a $28.00 price objective on Finisar and gave the stock a buy rating in a research note on Thursday, December 14th. Goldman Sachs downgraded Finisar from a neutral rating to a sell rating and dropped their price objective for the stock from $22.74 to $16.00 in a research note on Monday, January 15th. Finally, Barclays set a $25.00 price objective on Finisar and gave the stock a hold rating in a research note on Thursday, January 11th. Two analysts have rated the stock with a sell rating, seven have issued a hold rating and ten have assigned a buy rating to the company. Finisar currently has a consensus rating of Hold and a consensus target price of $24.56. 
Shares of Finisar ( NASDAQ FNSR ) traded down $0.47 during mid-day trading on Monday, reaching $15.70. The company’s stock had a trading volume of 5,148,546 shares, compared to its average volume of 4,459,911. The company has a quick ratio of 3.24, a current ratio of 4.06 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.29. Finisar has a one year low of $15.55 and a one year high of $29.07. The firm has a market cap of $1,868.38, a price-to-earnings ratio of 18.26, a PEG ratio of 2.47 and a beta of 1.02. 
Finisar (NASDAQ:FNSR) last announced its quarterly earnings results on Thursday, March 8th. The technology company reported $0.20 earnings per share (EPS) for the quarter, missing the Zacks’ consensus estimate of $0.23 by ($0.03). Finisar had a return on equity of 5.97% and a net margin of 7.35%. The business had revenue of $332.40 million for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $333.15 million. During the same quarter last year, the firm posted $0.59 EPS. The company’s revenue was down 12.7% compared to the same quarter last year. analysts predict that Finisar will post 0.47 EPS for the current year.

Finisar Company Profile 
Finisar Corporation (Finisar) is a provider of optical subsystems and components that are used in data communication and telecommunication applications. The Company’s optical subsystems consist of transmitters, receivers, transceivers, transponders and active optical cables, which provide the fundamental optical-electrical or optoelectronic interface for interconnecting the electronic equipment used in these networks, including the switches, routers, and servers used in wireline networks.
